Brewing guide

How to brew Vietnamese phin coffee at home

All you need is a phin filter, the right grind and a few minutes. This is how we brew phin coffee every day, from hot black coffee to iced milk coffee.

What you need

  • A single-cup aluminium or stainless-steel phin filter.
  • 20–25g of phin-ground coffee (about 3 heaped teaspoons): medium, slightly coarse, like coarse sand.
  • 100–120ml of just-boiled water, left for about 30 seconds so it's 90–96°C.
  • A heatproof glass; condensed milk and ice for iced milk coffee.

How to brew phin coffee, step by step

  1. Warm the phin and glass with hot water, then pour that water away.
  2. Add the coffee and shake gently to level it. Put the press on top and push lightly; don't pack it hard.
  3. Bloom: pour in about 20–25ml of hot water, just enough to wet all the grounds. Wait 30–45 seconds while the coffee swells.
  4. Top up to near the rim (about 80–100ml) and put the lid on.
  5. Let it drip for 4–6 minutes, ideally 1–2 drops per second.
  6. Enjoy it hot, pour it over ice for cà phê đen đá, or stir in 2–3 spoons of condensed milk and add ice for cà phê sữa đá.

Dripping too fast or too slow?

What you seeUsual causeFix
Done in under 3 minutes, weak coffeeGrind too coarse, too little coffee, press too looseGrind a little finer, add coffee, press a bit firmer
Over 7 minutes or clogged, harsh and bitterGrind too fine, packed too hardGrind coarser, press more gently

Which coffee is best for phin?

Phin coffee is best with plenty of Robusta and a darker roast. Đông (dark roast) gives the bold, traditional phin taste; Thu (medium-dark) is sweeter and lovely with milk. Choose 100% Robusta, or blend in 20–30% Arabica for more aroma. If you buy ground coffee, pick Ground and add "phin grind" in your order notes.

Tips for a better cup

  • For iced milk coffee, use 25g of coffee, since the ice dilutes it.
  • Use filtered water for a cleaner taste.
  • Use the coffee within 60 days of opening and keep the bag sealed.
